4. // PageAligned<T> — Specifications
5. //
6. // `PageAligned<T>` is a validated newtype wrapping a memory address (`int`)
7. // carrying the static guarantee that the address lies on a page boundary. Its
8. // abstract value is exactly that address (`PageAligned@ : int`, defined by the
9. // `View` impl in `page.rs`); the page-alignment fact is the property `inv()`
10. // over that value.
11. //
12. // `spec_addr` is the ghost projection of an arbitrary `T: Address` to its
13. // abstract address (`int`). It exists for *every* `T: Address` so that the
14. // `View` impl for `PageAligned<T>` — and hence the `@`-based contracts of the
15. // in-scope exec functions (`into_raw_value`, `from_address`) — can be stated
16. // for a bare `T: Address`, without the `T: View<V = int>` bound that would
17. //   * be unsatisfiable in a normal `cargo build` (the address-family `View`
18. //     impls are all `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated), and
19. //   * not be available on the generic exec `impl<T: Address> ...` blocks (and
20. //     would break `region.rs`, which uses `PageAligned<T>: Address` for a bare
21. //     `T: Address`).
22. // It is left uninterpreted here; the exec contracts pin it operationally
23. // (`into_raw_value` returns exactly `self@`), exactly as the sibling
24. // `FrameAddress::into_raw_value` trust boundary draws the same newtype-identity
25. // fact for the concrete frame address. It is `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated
26. // (ghost-only), so it does not exist in a normal build.
27. 
28. verus! {
29. 
30. // Ghost projection of any address to its abstract value (`int`).
31. pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>(addr: &T) -> int;
32. 
33. // `<PageAligned<T> as Address>::into_raw_value` is a method of the external
34. // `sys::mm::Address` trait. A trait-impl method cannot be body-verified in place
35. // without marking the whole `impl Address for PageAligned<T>` verified, which
36. // pulls every sibling method into scope and currently triggers a Verus
37. // front-end limitation (`vir/src/traits.rs` assertion). It is therefore specced
38. // here with `assume_specification`, mirroring the trust boundary the codebase
39. // already draws for `<PageAligned<T> as Address>::from_raw_value`
40. // (`kframe.spec.rs`) and `::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE` (`frame.rs`). The bound is
41. // exactly `T: Address` (matching the external signature), and the `@`-based
42. // contract is expressible because `PageAligned<T>: View` now holds for every
43. // `T: Address`. The real proof obligation is the inner
44. // `<T as Address>::into_raw_value` newtype identity, discharged when the
45. // `Address` trait itself is verified.
46. //
47. // Pure newtype identity projection: the returned raw `usize` is exactly the
48. // abstract address. Callers' in-page offset math and page walking require an
49. // identity projection (no masking/shifting).
50. pub assume_specification<T: Address> [
51.     <PageAligned<T> as Address>::into_raw_value
52. ](addr: PageAligned<T>) -> (result: usize)
53.     ensures
54.         result as int == addr@,
55. ;
56. 
57. } // verus!

11. ### Verification-order targets (only functions in scope)
12. | Function | Visibility | External call sites | Internal call sites |
13. |----------|-----------|--------------------:|--------------------:|
14. | `PageAligned::from_address` | `pub` | 20 | 5 |
15. | `PageAligned::into_raw_value` (`impl Address`) | trait-pub | 62 | 1 |
16. | `PageAligned<T>` (type) | `pub` | 176 references | — |

18. These three are the heaviest-used surface of the module: `from_address` is the
19. sole aligned-constructor, `into_raw_value` is the dominant read accessor, and
20. `PageAligned<T>` is threaded through almost every memory-management subsystem
21. (`mm::phys`, `mm::virt`, `pm::process`, `hal::io::mmio`, `hal::arch::…mmu`).
22. 
23. ## Trait Obligations
24. 
25. - Trait `Address` (`src/libs/sys/src/sys/mm/address/mod.rs`) — `PageAligned<T>`
26.   implements it by delegating to the inner `T: Address`. Caller-relevant members:
27.   - `into_raw_value(self) -> usize` — expected to return the underlying numeric
28.     address with **no transformation** (newtype identity). Callers subtract two
29.     raw values to get in-page offsets and add `PAGE_SIZE` multiples to walk pages,
30.     so the result must equal the abstract address.
31.   - `from_raw_value(raw) -> Result<Self, Error>` — delegates to
32.     `from_address(T::from_raw_value(raw)?)`; inherits the page-alignment check.
33.   - Supertraits `Eq`/`Ord`/`Debug` — `PageAligned` forwards `eq`/`cmp` to the
34.     inner value, so ordering/equality must agree with the underlying address.
35. - Trait `Deref<Target = T>` — compiler-dispatched; lets callers transparently use
36.   inner-`T` (`VirtualAddress`/`PhysicalAddress`) methods on a `PageAligned`.
37. 
38. ## Caller Expectations
39. 
40. ### `PageAligned::from_address(addr: T) -> Result<Self, Error>`
41. Representative callers: `hal/mem/types/region.rs:340`, `mm/virt/vmem.rs:978/1053/1356`,
42. `mm/elf.rs:284`, `hal/mem/types/address/frame.rs:78/86`,
43. `hal/arch/shared/mem/mmu/page_{directory,table}.rs`.
44. 
45. - Callers assume on **success** (`Ok`): the wrapped address is page-aligned, i.e.
46.   `result@ % PAGE_SIZE == 0`. This is the invariant the whole type exists to carry;
47.   downstream code (e.g. offset math, frame/page conversions, MMU mapping) relies on
48.   it without re-checking.
49. - Callers assume the returned value's address is **unchanged** — `from_address`
50.   validates, it does not round/normalize. The result's raw value equals `addr`'s
51.   raw value (`result@ == addr@`).
52. - Many callers pre-align with `align_down(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)` then call
53.   `from_address(...)?` (e.g. `vmem.rs`, `identity_map.rs:417`); they treat the `?`
54.   as "can't fail because I just aligned", but still rely on the alignment guarantee.
55. - Callers assume on **failure** (`Err`): `Error::BadAddress` when `addr` is not
56.   page-aligned, with no side effects (value-type, nothing to roll back).
57. - Callers **don't care about**: the internal newtype representation
58.   (`struct PageAligned<T>(T)`), the exact error message string, or how the
59.   alignment check is implemented (`addr.is_aligned(PAGE_ALIGNMENT)`).
60. 
61. ### `PageAligned::into_raw_value(self) -> usize` (impl `Address`)
62. Representative callers: `mm/virt/vmem.rs` offset math (`:979,1054,1186,1357,1363`),
63. `hal/io/mmio/allocator.rs:189/193`, `hal/arch/.../xapic.rs`, `ioapic.rs:78`,
64. `pm/process/manager/unsafe.rs:381/382`, `mm/virt/manager.rs:633`.
65. 
66. - Callers assume the returned `usize` **equals the abstract address**
67.   (`result as int == self@`) — pure identity projection, no masking/shifting. This
68.   is critical: `vaddr.into_raw_value() - page_aligned.into_raw_value()` must yield
69.   the true in-page offset (`0..PAGE_SIZE`), and `addr.into_raw_value() + k*PAGE_SIZE`
70.   must address the k-th following page.
71. - Because `self` is page-aligned, callers further assume `result % PAGE_SIZE == 0`
72.   (used implicitly when the result is fed to MMIO base registers, `*mut u8` casts at
73.   `vmem.rs:1419`, and re-wrapped via `from_raw_value`).
74. - Callers assume it is **total** (no `Result`) and **side-effect free** (consumes
75.   `self` by value).
76. - Callers **don't care about** whether the value comes from `VirtualAddress` or
77.   `PhysicalAddress` inner storage — only that it round-trips with `from_raw_value`.

80. - Callers use it as a **type-level proof token**: holding a
81.   `PageAligned<VirtualAddress>` / `PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>` means "this address

83.   signatures (`region.start()`, `MmioRegion::base()`, `UserStack::base()/top()`,
84.   `Vmem` user/kernel address checks, process-manager APIs).
85. - Conversions callers rely on: `into_inner()` (unwrap to inner `T`, 21 sites),
86.   `into_virtual_address()` / `into_physical_address()` (alignment-preserving
87.   P↔V conversion), and `Deref` to reach inner-address helpers.
88. - Callers **don't care about** the single-field tuple-struct layout, only that the
89.   alignment invariant is preserved by every operation that returns a `PageAligned`.

91. ## Abstract Resource
92. `PageAligned<T>` is a **validated wrapper around a memory address (`int`) that
93. guarantees the address lies on a page boundary**. It is the kernel's compile-time
94. witness of page alignment, threaded through physical/virtual memory management,
95. MMU paging, MMIO regions, and process stacks.

1. # View Design: `hal::mem::types::address::aligned::page` (`PageAligned<T>`)
2. 
3. > Scope: design/refine the abstract `View` for `PageAligned<T>` that the
4. > in-scope functions (`PageAligned::from_address`, `PageAligned::into_raw_value`,
5. > and the `PageAligned<T>` type itself) will reference in later spec/proof phases.
6. >
7. > A `View`/`inv` skeleton already exists in the module's `verus!` block. This
8. > document **reviews and confirms** that skeleton against the caller analysis,
9. > applies the substitution test to each field, and records the rationale and the
10. > alternatives that were rejected. The conclusion is that the existing design is
11. > correct as-is; no change to the View shape is warranted.
12. 
13. ---
14. 
15. ## Abstract Resource
16. 
17. `PageAligned<T>` is, to its callers, **a memory address (a single mathematical
18. integer) carrying the static guarantee that the address lies on a page
19. boundary**. It is the kernel's compile-time witness of page alignment, threaded
20. through physical/virtual memory management, MMU paging, MMIO regions, and
21. process stacks. The wrapped `T` (`VirtualAddress` / `PhysicalAddress`) is itself
22. viewed as an `int` address, so a `PageAligned<T>` adds no new observable state —
23. only a new *property* (alignment) over the same single address value.
24. 
25. ---
26. 
27. ## View Struct
28. 
29. The abstract state of a `PageAligned<T>` is exactly one value: the underlying
30. numeric address, as an unbounded integer. Verus models this with a scalar
31. `View` (`type V = int`) rather than a record struct, because there is only one
32. caller-observable quantity.
33. 
34. ```rust
35. impl<T: Address> View for PageAligned<T> {
36.     type V = int;
37. 
38.     // The abstract address (raw numeric address as an unbounded integer).
39.     // Delegates to the inner address's ghost projection `spec_addr` — newtype
40.     // identity.
41.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
42.         spec_addr(&self.0)
43.     }
44. }
45. ```
46. 
47. > **Bound change (this phase).** The skeleton bounded the impl on
48. > `T: Address + View<V = int>` and defined `view = self.0@`. That bound is
49. > **unusable for the in-scope exec contracts**: the `@`-based ensures of
50. > `into_raw_value` (a method of the generic `impl<T: Address> Address for
51. > PageAligned<T>`) and of `from_address` must be expressible for a *bare*
52. > `T: Address`, and the `View<V = int>` bound (a) is not present on those exec
53. > impls, (b) cannot be added to them without breaking `region.rs`
54. > (`TruncatedMemoryRegion<T>` uses `PageAligned<T>: Address` for bare
55. > `T: Address`), and (c) is **unsatisfiable in a normal `cargo build`** because
56. > every address-family `View` impl is `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated, so a normal
57. > build that saw the bound would fail (`PhysicalAddress: View not satisfied`).
58. >
59. > The fix keeps the same abstract resource but makes the `View` **unconditional**
60. > over `T: Address`, delegating to a ghost projection
61. > `pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T: Address>(addr: &T) -> int` (declared in
62. > `page.spec.rs`, `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated). `spec_addr` is uninterpreted;
63. > the exec contract `into_raw_value: result as int == self@` pins it
64. > operationally (newtype identity), exactly as the sibling
65. > `FrameAddress::into_raw_value` trust boundary does for the concrete frame
66. > address. Because `view()` is `closed`, the switch from `self.0@` to
67. > `spec_addr(&self.0)` is invisible to every consumer (including `FrameAddress`
68. > and `region.rs`, whose own views are `closed`), and broadening the bound from
69. > `T: Address + View` to `T: Address` only *adds* availability.
70. 
71. Equivalent "single-field" reading:
72. 
73. ```rust
74. pub struct PageAlignedView {
75.     // addr: the numeric memory address this token denotes, as `int`.
76.     //       The only state a caller can observe; the page-boundary fact is a
77.     //       *property* of this value, expressed by inv(), not a separate field.
78.     addr: int,
79. }
80. ```
81. 
82. `view()` is `closed`: callers reference `p@` as an `int`, but the mapping
83. (`spec_addr(&self.0)`, i.e. delegation through the inner `T`'s ghost
84. projection) does not leak. Because `spec_addr` is defined for every
85. `T: Address`, the wrapper has a `View` without requiring `T: View<V = int>`,
86. which is what makes the in-scope `@`-based contracts expressible for a bare
87. `T: Address` (see the bound-change note above).
88. 
89. ---
90. 
91. ## Well-formedness Invariant
92. 
93. ```rust
94. impl<T: Address> PageAligned<T> {
95.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
96.         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
97.     }
98. }
99. ```
100. 
101. - `spec_page_size()` is the shared uninterpreted spec constant for the page size
102.   (declared in `hal::mem`, imported here as `crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size`,
103.   and tied to the exec `PAGE_SIZE` by an `assume_specification` in the sibling
104.   `frame.rs`). Using the abstract constant — not a literal `4096` — keeps the
105.   invariant independent of any concrete page size.
106. - `inv()` is `pub open`: it is the central caller-visible promise of the type
107.   ("this address is page-aligned"), so callers and downstream specs must be able
108.   to unfold it. This is the single property the whole type exists to carry, and
109.   it matches the existing `inv()` already in the module and the identical
110.   invariant on the sibling `FrameAddress`.
111. 
112. This is the only well-formedness condition. `int` is unbounded, so no
113. non-negativity or upper-bound clause is needed at the View level; range facts
114. (`0 ≤ addr ≤ max_addr`) belong to the inner `T`'s own invariant, not to the
115. alignment wrapper, and adding them here would duplicate `T`'s contract.
116. 
117. ---
118. 
119. ## Spec Transition Functions
120. 
121. `PageAligned<T>` is an immutable value newtype: every operation is a pure
122. projection or a pure validated construction. There is no mutable state and thus
123. no pre/post state machine — the "transitions" are deterministic relations
124. between input views and output views. They are stated below as the contracts the
125. later spec phase will attach (no extra `pub spec fn` is added to
126. `impl PageAligned`, per the view-design rule; these are the ensures the
127. functions will carry).
128. 
129. ### `from_address(addr: T) -> Result<Self, Error>`  *(in scope)*
130. 
131. A *partial, identity-preserving, validating* constructor.
132. 
133. ```text
134. // Success: identity-preserving and establishes the invariant.
135. result is Ok(p)  ==>  p@ == spec_addr(&addr)  &&  p.inv()   // p@ % spec_page_size() == 0
136. // Failure: exactly the unaligned case, no normalization, no side effects.
137. result is Err(_) ==>  spec_addr(&addr) % spec_page_size() != 0
138. // Liveness (aligned => Ok) is NOT a separate clause: it is the contrapositive of
139. // the total `Err => unaligned` arm above, so it is omitted as subsumed.
140. ```
141. 
142. Notes:
143. - `spec_addr(&addr)` is the abstract address of the input `T`; for the wrapped
144.   result `p`, `p@ == spec_addr(&p.0) == spec_addr(&addr)` since `p.0 == addr`.
145. - `from_address` **validates, it never rounds/normalizes**: on success the
146.   address is unchanged (`p@ == addr@`). This matches callers that pre-align with
147.   `align_down` and then treat `?` as infallible while still relying on the
148.   alignment guarantee.
